items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I got myself together and got started with Jim Hall.

ctx.x: I left Lena there. My mother became ill and I decided to come home, and as it was she lingered about seven or eight months before she passed. But when I left Lena I came back to LA and I was going to get a trio together. I was going to get Gerry Wiggins, but all these guys, man they had their own thing going so that just 86’d that. So I got myself together and got started with Jim Hall.

Now we’re really getting into the -- we’re going to stop. So, you know, during the break I just wanted to, or now that we’re off break I wanted to come back and fill in a few more of the chronological gaps. One of the biographies mentions when you got out of the military, that you actually joined Jimmy Mundy and then got stranded in Salt Lake City.

items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So that’s how I hooked up with Chico, and that was amazing.

ctx.x: Wow. If you have any other particular memories about the rehearsal band and who some of the people were in those (overlapping/inaudible) …

Yeah, there were some terrific musicians. My friend’s name is… I’m not sure he’s still around. You found him for me about ten years… Joe Dolny, D-O-L-N-Y. Some great musicians. In fact, Mel Lewis was… Oh, I don’t know if he was actually in that band, but [Joe?] ended up on a record date with a bunch of guys from Kenton’s band, and Mel Lewis was playing drums and everything. And there was a French horn player in the band whose name I may remember sometime. And he was studying… Anyway, I was at the French horn…
Let’s talk a little bit about that quintet, because historically it was very innovative and unique and…

items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: Jim Hall was just a stroke of luck. He needed a gig and he heard that I was organizing, putting a group together.

ctx.x: That sound with the cello and pianoless. Did that come about from sitting down and thinking let’s find something different here? Or was it a more practical—

Originally the group was going to be French horn, John Graas, he was the number one French horn player on the West Coast at that time when I formed the group. The group was intact with Buddy and Jim Hall, and Carson. And Buddy and I came up musically together. Cars and I were with Gerry together, and Jim Hall was just a stroke of luck. He needed a gig and he heard that I was organizing, putting a group together. Because he was stacking music in a music store at that time. He wasn’t even playing. And the day of…
And even had the part where the stick fell.
